Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Power Holdings Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Power Holdings' Q3 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Torres, Chief Operating Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Strategy Officer; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
    1.  Management's perspectives on key industry trends and challenges.
    2.  O&M expense management initiatives and efficiency gains.
    3.  Progress towards clean energy goals and emission reductions.
    4.  Overview of financial performance relative to guidance.
    5.  Rate base growth and factors impacting growth.
    6.  Updates on regulatory rate case filings and outcomes.

Let me provide some more detail on these six key aspects, starting with our view of the broader industry landscape.

Before we dive deeper, I'd like to share our perspectives on the utilities and power generation sector. We're in a transformative era marked by surging electricity demand, rapid decarbonization efforts, and ongoing supply chain issues. At Apex Power Holdings, with our diversified 25 GW fleet spanning natural gas, renewables, nuclear, and storage across the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic, we're well-positioned to seize opportunities and tackle headwinds.

Demand growth is exploding, per the EIA's latest outlook, with U.S. power needs rising 4.7% annually through 2050—double historical rates. Data centers from AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft drove nearly 20% of new load in PJM and ERCOT last year, lifting peaks 12-15% YoY. In our markets, we've secured 2.5 GW of 15-year PPAs with tech firms at prices 25% above our trailing average. Electrification via IRA tax credits has EVs up 40% YoY, and CHIPS Act reshoring adds 50 TWh by 2030 per NREL.

This fuels the renewables and storage boom: 510 GW global additions in 2023, 35 GW U.S., mostly solar and wind. BESS deployments jumped 75% to 12 GW in North America, with IRRs now 8-10% as LCOE drops below $30/MWh. Our 1.2 GW BESS pipeline, like the 300 MW/1,200 MWh Dragonfly project in Texas next to gas peakers, is 95% contracted at peak factors. LDES tech from Form Energy could handle California's 2 GW curtailments.

Decarbonization drives $1.2 trillion in capex since 2020, with nuclear restarts like Three Mile Island for Microsoft paving for 5-10 GW SMRs and extensions. Our 50% Southeast Hydrogen Hub stake enables 20-30% H2 blending in gas turbines. Regionally, ERCOT's 40% renewables bring volatility—$5B uplift last summer; PJM's 2,700 GW queue shortens via FERC 2020; CAISO fights solar erosion; MISO risks shortfalls post-20 GW coal retirements; Europe's REPowerEU boosts offshore wind, where we hold 200 MW North Sea.

Challenges persist: supply chains delay transformers 3-4 years, costs up 150%; interconnection at $300/kW; FERC ROE caps; yields at 4.2% hike premiums; capex intensity high. Nat gas at $2.50/MMBtu aids our 62% heat rate turbines; we've spent $150M on cybersecurity like AI anomaly detection.

Our strategy: 40% capex to renewables/storage, 30% gas-to-H2, 20% nuclear uprates. JVs with NextEra and Fluence save 15% on EPC; VPPs via Apex GridEdge add $50M EBITDA. Demand-supply gaps create opportunities; our A- rating, 12% FFO/debt, 45% renewables by 2027 target 6-8% EPS growth.

To build on our operational efficiencies, I'll turn it over to Sarah Jenkins, our CFO, to cover O&M management, financial results, clean energy progress, rate base, and regulatory updates.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning, everyone. Let's start with O&M expense management, a core driver of our margins. O&M represents 20-30% of costs in our sector, amid gas volatility, EPA rules, and net-zero shifts like California's SB 100.

Q3 O&M was $285 million, down 6.8% YoY or $21 million below guidance midpoint—the third straight decline, TTM at $1.12 billion, down 8.2%. Ex-coal remediation, core drop 7.5%, boosting EBITDA to $450 million, up 12% YoY, ahead of NextEra and Duke.

Plant optimization drove 40% of savings: PJM CCGT heat rates improved 1.8% to 7,315 Btu/kWh via Siemens digital upgrades on GE 7HA units, cutting NOx, adding 15 MW/unit. Gas outages fell to 1.2% with FLIR drones, saving 25 days.

Coal (15% of 12 GW regulated): $4.2 million saved via Emerson digital twins on supercritical units, trimming SCR costs 12%, extending ESP life. Midwest O&M to $28/kW-month vs. EIA peers.

Renewables (35% post-800 MW ERCOT add): Stem Athena AI on 1.5 GW solar hit 98.7% availability, O&M down 11% to $14,500/MW; Nordex cleaners on SPP wind cut AEP losses to 1.8%, saving $2.8 million.

Workforce/supply chain: 7% headcount cut via upskilling to 25.4 orders/FTE; Maverick sourcing fixed oils/transformers vs. 22% copper rise.

O&M/sales to 22%; expect 5% FY24 decline, $80-100 million savings by 2026 via Bentley APM. This embeds resilience in our 12 GW portfolio.

Shifting to our overall financial performance relative to guidance. Revenues hit $2.85 billion, beating $2.7 billion midpoint by 5.6% or $155 million, on 8% higher sales to 28.5 million MWh and rate recovery. Adjusted EBITDA $1.12 billion, up 6.7% over $1.05 billion guidance, via 92% hedged gas at $3.25/MMBtu vs. $4.80 spot.

EPS $1.47, topping $1.35-1.40 range—eighth straight beat, with $85 million AFUDC from $4.2 billion capex like Blackhawk BESS and Virginia offshore wind. FCF $650 million supports $0.85 dividend, $300 million buybacks.

Regulated utilities (42%): $1.45 billion revenue, +7%, 4% beat on PA/NJ rates at 9.4% ROE on $12.5 billion base; sales +6% to 18.2 million MWh on HDD, data centers. Margins +220 bps to 42% via AMI.

Competitive gen: thermal $520 million, +3%, 68% factor, PJM $240/kW clears. Nuclear 92% factor dip; renewables 4.8 million MWh, -12% on weather, but hedged $120/MWh, BESS $45 million. ERCOT strong; PJM queues; CAISO capex.

Balance sheet: 3.4x net debt/EBITDA, $2.8 billion liquidity, BBB+/Baa2. Raising FY24: revenue $11.2-11.5 billion, EBITDA $4.45-4.55 billion, EPS $5.75-5.85.

Now, rate base growth, key to earnings. At $28.4 billion end-Q3, +7.2% YoY, 2.1% sequential—strongest in years on $2.8 billion capex, $2.2 billion deployed, CWIP +15% to $1.9 billion.

Drivers: T&D 55%, $850 million add via GridFlex 2030—300 miles reconductoring, 120 miles energized, $22 million AFUDC. Renewables 30%, 420 MW solar like Prairie Wind, 2.8 points growth; 1.2 GW BESS adds $1.1 billion. Gen 15%, $250 million gas uprates offset coal.

Tailwinds: KY $1.2 billion rider, 85% CWIP; $65 million AFUDC. Headwinds: dep up 9%, debt 4.6%; transformer delays.

Target 6-8% growth, $10 billion five-year capex; reaffirmed $3.0-3.2 billion, year-end $30.2 billion.

On clean energy progress under Vision 2040 net-zero by 2040: CO2 intensity -18% to 285 MT/GWh, ahead of 2025 target; Scope 1/2 -12% to 14.2 million MT on coal retirements; Scope 3 -7%.

Renewables 42% of 28 GW, +1.8 GW YTD: 750 MW Southwest solar (First Solar, 28% factor); 450 MW Plains wind (Vestas, 45%); 200 MW VA offshore. Storage: 350 MWh LFP, $45 million ancillaries; ESS iron-flow pilot.

CCUS on CCGT at 90% capture, $40/ton path; H2 blending 20%; nuclear +150 MW. $2.1 billion clean capex (65%), IRRs 12-15%, $450 million IRA credits, $120 million RECs.

68% to 2030 goals; FY24 2 GW adds, 260 MT/GWh. Buffers vs. risks.

Regulatory updates: Proactive filings support 65% EBITDA regulated. Indiana IURC $285 million on $4.75 billion base settled black-box: 9.75% ROE, $212 million phased, fuel rider—ROE to 9.4%.

Ohio PUCO $175 million: 98% grant, 10.0% ROE +50 bps, $168 million, multi-year to 2026. Kentucky PSC $310 million pending Q4, optimistic 9.5% ROE, coal securitization.

FERC MISO true-up: 10.25% ROE +100 bps, $45 million. Midwest ROEs 9.7%; funds $2.8 billion capex, regulatory lag <9 months.

Q3 capex $700 million, focused on renewables and grid modernization. Balance sheet strong; FY24 mid-single digit EPS growth.

Now, back to Johnathan.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Sarah. Great detail there.

Michael Torres: Thank you, Sarah. Operationally, we're seeing improved efficiency in our combined-cycle gas turbine plants due to AI-optimized controls. This has resulted in a 5% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 20%.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Michael. Strategically, we're exploring battery storage opportunities. This will drive future growth. We're evaluating acquisitions in the ERCOT market.

Dr. Raj Patel: Thank you, Elena. Technologically, we're investing in grid modernization and cybersecurity. We recently deployed an AI-driven anomaly detection platform to bolster defenses.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Sarah, Michael, Elena, and Raj. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for rate base growth?

Johnathan Hale: Certainly. As Sarah outlined, we're targeting 6-8% annual growth through robust capex in T&D, renewables, and gen optimizations, with strong regulatory support minimizing lag.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Gonzalez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Gonzalez: What is your outlook for commodity prices?

Sarah Jenkins: We have 92% of gas hedged at favorable levels, positioning us well even if spots remain elevated, supporting our raised guidance.

Operator: Our next question comes from Chris Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Chris Patel: How are you mitigating supply chain risks?

Michael Torres: Through long-term contracts, digital twins for maintenance, and diversified suppliers, as seen in our O&M gains and project timelines.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in Q3, demonstrating the strength of our business model and commitment to long-term shareholder value. We're focused on executing priorities and positioning Apex Power Holdings for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
